# Copilot Instructions

This repository is a **collector** for one macroeconomic data source. Every
collector repository in this fleet — present and future — must follow the
patterns documented here. This pilot (`collector_banxico_encuesta`) is the
canonical reference; new collectors are generated by copying its shape and
swapping in source-specific extract logic.

The goal is a fleet of small, boring, identical-looking repositories that any
non-expert can read and modify. Standardization is the feature.

---

## 1. Repository Layout (canonical)

Every collector repository must look like this. Do not invent new top-level
directories or new modules in `scripts/` unless a real source-specific need
demands it.

```
collector_<source>_<dataset>/
├── .env.example         # Documented; .env is gitignored
├── .gitignore           # __pycache__/, .venv/, .env (and nothing else by default)
├── .github/
│   ├── copilot-instructions.md
│   ├── prompts/
│   └── skills/
├── .vscode/
│   ├── launch.json      # Debug current file + remote attach
│   └── settings.json
├── README.md            # Quickstart only — no architecture essays
├── main.py              # Pipeline orchestrator (lives at the root)
├── pyproject.toml       # Project metadata + dependencies
├── requirements.txt     # Pinned floor versions, mirrors pyproject
└── scripts/
    ├── __init__.py      # Empty
    ├── config.py        # Env-driven settings + manual .env loader
    ├── db.py            # SQLAlchemy engine factory (PROD vs local)
    ├── init_db.py       # CREATE SCHEMA / TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
    ├── extract.py       # Fetch + parse the source → {ref_date: {series_id: value}}
    ├── metadata.py      # Step 1: upsert standardized metadata table
    ├── time_series.py   # Step 2: upsert time_series with vintage tracking
    └── run_logs.py      # Persist one log row per run
```

**Rules:**

- `main.py` lives at the **repo root**, not inside `scripts/`. The pipeline
  orchestrator is the entry point; everything in `scripts/` is a building block.
- `scripts/` is a flat, file-per-responsibility package. No subpackages, no
  base classes, no abstract collectors, no plugins.
- Every collector has its own `.env`, its own schema, and its own copy of
  these eight files. Do not extract a shared library.
- Tests are not part of the pilot. Add a `tests/` folder only when a specific
  collector has logic complex enough to justify it.

---

## 2. Standardized Output Schema (do not deviate)

Every collector writes exactly three tables in its own schema. The DDL is
portable between PostgreSQL (local dev) and Databricks SQL (production).

**Catalog / schema convention:**

- Catalog: `macrobond_inhouse` (Databricks production).
- Schema: `collector_<source>_<dataset>` — must match the repo name.

### `metadata`

One row per series. Idempotent upsert: unchanged rows keep their old
`collected_at`; only new or modified series are written.

| Column              | Type            | Notes                              |
| ------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `series_id`         | VARCHAR(200) PK | Structured ID, see §4              |
| `name`              | VARCHAR(500)    | Human-readable English name        |
| `description`       | VARCHAR(2000)   |                                    |
| `country`           | VARCHAR(3)      | ISO 4217 currency or 3-letter code |
| `frequency`         | VARCHAR(20)     | `daily`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, … |
| `unit`              | VARCHAR(50)     | `percent`, `index`, `number`, …    |
| `first_observation` | DATE            |                                    |
| `last_observation`  | DATE            |                                    |
| `observation_count` | INTEGER         |                                    |
| `collected_at`      | TIMESTAMP       |                                    |

### `time_series`

Append-only, vintage-tracked observations.

| Column           | Type             | Notes                                   |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `id`             | BIGINT IDENTITY  | PK                                      |
| `series_id`      | VARCHAR(200)     |                                         |
| `reference_date` | DATE             | Date the observation refers to          |
| `vintage_date`   | DATE             | Publication date of *this* version      |
| `value`          | DOUBLE PRECISION |                                         |
| `collected_at`   | TIMESTAMP        |                                         |

Unique constraint: `(series_id, reference_date, vintage_date)`.

**Vintage rules — these are non-negotiable:**

- First time we see `(series_id, reference_date)`: INSERT one row with
  `vintage_date = today` (the collection date — **never** the reference
  date). A backfill pulled today must not masquerade as knowledge
  available on the historical reference date.
- Value unchanged on a later run: no-op (do not touch `collected_at`).
- Value changed on a later run — compare `today` against the latest
  stored row's `vintage_date`:
  - `today` is **later**: INSERT a new row with `vintage_date = today`.
  - `today` **equals** it (same-day revision): UPDATE that row's
    `value` and `collected_at` in place. A `DATE` vintage cannot hold
    two same-day revisions as separate rows; the latest collection of
    the day wins. Intraday history within a vintage day is not
    retained.

See GUIDELINES.md §3 for the full as-of query contract and the
exclusion for collectors that need intraday preservation.

### `logs`

One row per `main.py` run.

| Column        | Type            | Notes                                |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `id`          | BIGINT IDENTITY | PK                                   |
| `started_at`  | TIMESTAMP       |                                      |
| `finished_at` | TIMESTAMP       |                                      |
| `status`      | VARCHAR(20)     | `success` \| `error`                 |
| `log_text`    | VARCHAR(65535)  | Captured stdout, truncated if needed |
| `traceback`   | VARCHAR(65535)  | NULL on success                      |

The log row is written in `main.py`'s `finally` block so failures are still
recorded. Truncate text fields client-side before insert (see `run_logs.py`).

---

## 3. The Eight Modules — Responsibilities

Each module has **one job**. Keep them small (the pilot is < 1200 lines total).

### `scripts/config.py` (~60 lines)

- Manually parse `.env` from the repo root — **do not add `python-dotenv`**.
- Expose constants for `SCHEMA_NAME`, `CATALOG_NAME`, table names,
  `START_DATE_LOOKBACK_MONTHS`, `PROD`, `DATABASE_URL`,
  `DEFAULT_START_DATE`, HTTP tuning (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `DOWNLOAD_DELAY`,
  `MAX_RETRIES`, `BACKOFF_FACTOR`, `USER_AGENT`), `LOG_LEVEL`.
- All settings have safe defaults; users only need to set `COLLECTOR_DB_URL`
  (or `PROD=True`).

### `scripts/db.py` (~60 lines)

- Single function: `build_engine() -> Engine`.
- `PROD=True` → `kinea_database.sql.get_orm_engine(catalog, schema)`.
- `PROD=False` → `create_engine(DATABASE_URL, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800)`.
- Redact credentials before logging the URL.
- **No DDL here.** Schema and table creation lives in `init_db.py`.

### `scripts/init_db.py` (~100 lines)

- DDL constants: `CREATE_SCHEMA`, `CREATE_METADATA_TABLE`,
  `CREATE_TIME_SERIES_TABLE`, `CREATE_LOGS_TABLE` — all wrapped in
  `IF NOT EXISTS`.
- Function: `init_db(engine)`. Called automatically by `main.py` on every run.
- Also runnable as a script (`python -m scripts.init_db`) to bootstrap a fresh
  database manually.
- DDL must be valid on **both** PostgreSQL and Databricks SQL. When in doubt,
  pick the lowest common subset (e.g. `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`,
  `DOUBLE PRECISION`, `VARCHAR(N)`).

### `scripts/extract.py` (the only source-specific module)

- Returns one thing: `dict[date, dict[str, float | None]]`
  — `{reference_date: {series_id: value}}`.
- HTTP via `httpx` with a built-in retry helper (`_http_get`) handling 429,
  5xx, and transport errors with exponential backoff.
- One `httpx.Client` per `collect_raw_data()` call (context-managed).
- Define source-specific constants at the top: `SOURCE_NAME`, `BASE_URL`,
  parsing layout (rows to skip, column ranges, header strings), code maps.
- Soft failures (one bad date, one schema mismatch) **log a warning and
  skip** — they do not abort the run.
- Hard failures (auth, network down across all retries) propagate.

### `scripts/metadata.py` (~170 lines)

- `build_metadata_rows(parsed_by_date, collected_at)` — derive descriptive
  fields from `series_id` + first/last/count from observations.
- `upsert_metadata(engine, parsed_by_date, collected_at)` — SELECT existing,
  compare against `_COMPARABLE_COLUMNS`, INSERT new, UPDATE only changed.
  Returns `(inserted, updated)`.
- Names, descriptions, units are derived from the structured `series_id`
  using a small `parse_series_id` helper exported from `extract.py`.

### `scripts/time_series.py` (~200 lines)

- `get_max_reference_date(engine)` — used by `main.py` to compute the rewind
  window.
- `upsert_time_series(engine, parsed_by_date, collected_at)` — pulls the
  latest vintage per `(series_id, reference_date)` into a pandas DataFrame,
  left-merges against the request DataFrame, splits into new observations
  vs. new vintages, inserts in batches of 500.
- Use `ROUND_DECIMALS = 10` when comparing floats to avoid spurious "changed"
  matches from float round-trip noise.
- Returns `(new_observations, new_vintages)`.

### `scripts/run_logs.py` (~65 lines)

- `insert_run_log(engine, started_at, finished_at, status, log_text, traceback_text)`.
- Truncate `log_text` and `traceback_text` to 65535 chars with a clear
  `[...truncated...]` suffix.
- Best-effort: errors writing the log are logged, never raised. The pipeline
  must not fail because the log table is unreachable.

### `main.py` (~180 lines)

The only orchestrator. Responsibilities, in order:

1. Parse `--start-date` and `--log-level` via `argparse`.
2. Configure root logging with a dual handler: stdout + an in-memory
   `io.StringIO` buffer (this is what gets persisted to `logs.log_text`).
3. `build_engine()` → `init_db(engine)`.
4. Resolve start date: explicit override > `latest reference_date − N months` >
   `DEFAULT_START_DATE`.
5. `collect_raw_data(start_date)`.
6. `upsert_metadata(...)` then `upsert_time_series(...)`.
7. In a `try/except/finally`, capture status (`success`/`error`) and traceback,
   then write one row to `logs` regardless of outcome.

`main.py` should contain almost no business logic — just orchestration.

---

## 4. Series ID Convention

`series_id` must be a **structured, parseable, uppercase string** that uniquely
identifies one series within the collector. The structure is collector-specific
but always:

- Uppercase, segments joined by `_`.
- Components ordered from coarse to fine: `{TYPE}_{STAT}_{HORIZON}`,
  `{COUNTRY}_{INDICATOR}_{TRANSFORM}`, etc.
- Round-trippable: a `parse_series_id()` helper in `extract.py` decomposes
  the ID, and `metadata.py` uses that decomposition to derive `name`,
  `description`, and `unit`.

Never hand-write a name/description for each series. Derive them from the ID.

---

## 5. Idempotency & Reruns

The pipeline must be safe to run any number of times.

- `init_db()` runs every time and is a no-op when objects exist.
- Default behavior with no `--start-date` rewinds `START_DATE_LOOKBACK_MONTHS`
  (5) months from the latest stored `reference_date` to catch late revisions
  without re-downloading the full archive.
- Metadata: identical row → no write. Different row → UPDATE.
- Time series: identical value → no write. Different value → INSERT new
  vintage row.
- Two runs back-to-back must produce zero new metadata writes and zero new
  vintage rows.

---

## 6. Coding Style

- Python ≥ 3.11. `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of every
  module.
- Type hints on every function signature. `dict[...]`, `list[...]`,
  `X | None` PEP 604 syntax — no `Optional`, no `Dict`.
- Logging via `logging.getLogger(__name__)`. The format is set once in
  `main.py`: `%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s`. Never use
  `print` outside of a script's `__main__` block.
- Direct SQL via `sqlalchemy.text(...)` and named parameters
  (`:series_id`, `:value`, …). **No ORM models. No declarative base.** The
  schema lives in DDL strings, not Python classes.
- Module-level docstring on every file explaining what it does and why it
  exists. Function docstrings are short and describe behavior, not code.
- No comments restating the obvious; one short `# ──── section ────` divider
  per logical block in long files (see `extract.py`) is acceptable.
- Imports grouped: stdlib → third-party → local, blank lines between groups.
- No `try/except Exception` swallowing errors silently. Either log + skip
  (with a clear warning) or re-raise.

---

## 7. Dependencies

Keep the dependency list minimal and stable. The pilot uses **only**:

```
httpx>=0.27
beautifulsoup4>=4.12   # only if the source serves HTML
pandas>=2.0
openpyxl>=3.1          # only if the source serves Excel
sqlalchemy>=2.0
```

Optional production driver (`psycopg2-binary`) is commented out in
`requirements.txt` and exposed as an extra in `pyproject.toml`.

**Do not add:**

- `python-dotenv` — `config.py` parses `.env` manually (~10 lines).
- `requests` — use `httpx`.
- `pydantic`, `attrs`, `dataclasses-json` — plain dicts and tuples are fine.
- `alembic` or migration frameworks — the schema is forward-only and managed
  by `init_db.py`.
- A logging framework — stdlib `logging` is sufficient.
- `pytest` unless tests actually exist.

---

## 8. Self-Containment Principle

**Each collector owns its complete logic.** Source-specific quirks live in
that collector's `scripts/extract.py`. The standardized parts (`config.py`,
`db.py`, `init_db.py`, `metadata.py`, `time_series.py`, `run_logs.py`,
`main.py`) are nearly identical across repos by design — they are **copied
and lightly edited**, not imported from a shared package.

Why:

- Non-experts can read one repo end-to-end without crawling a shared library.
- A bug in the shared layer can't take down 50 collectors at once.
- Each collector can evolve independently when its source has unusual needs.

When you find yourself wanting to extract a "common" helper, **don't**.
Duplicate the 30 lines instead. Standardization is enforced by the
`build-collector` skill, not by Python imports.

---

## 9. Adding a New Collector

Use the `build-collector` skill (`.github/skills/build-collector/SKILL.md`).
It walks through copying the pilot, swapping in the new source's extract
logic, and verifying the standardized output. Do not improvise the structure.

For onboarding from a user request, use the `onboard-new-api` prompt
(`.github/prompts/onboard-new-api.prompt.md`).

---

## 10. Development Workflow Skills

These are general-purpose skills that apply to any change in any collector:

| Skill                    | When to Use                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `planning-and-design`    | Before any non-trivial change                                      |
| `research-first`         | Before writing custom code — check libs and the pilot first        |
| `test-driven-development`| When the change is complex enough to warrant tests                 |
| `systematic-debugging`   | Before proposing a fix for any bug                                 |
| `code-review`            | After completing features, before merging                          |
| `security-review`        | When touching credentials, HTTP, or SQL                            |
| `verification-loop`      | Before opening a PR                                                |
| `get-api-docs`           | Before writing code against any third-party API                    |
| `build-collector`        | When creating a new collector repository from scratch              |
| `audit-collector`        | When verifying a collector's metadata against the official source  |
| `series-selection`       | When choosing what series to include from a source                 |

### External API Documentation

When writing extract logic against any third-party API, use `get-api-docs`
(via the `chub` CLI or MCP tools) before coding. Source APIs change; do not
rely on training data.

---

## 11. What NOT to Do

The pilot was reached by deleting things. Maintain that discipline.

- ❌ Don't introduce a `BaseCollector` class or any inheritance hierarchy.
- ❌ Don't add a CLI framework (Click, Typer). `argparse` is enough.
- ❌ Don't add a config loader library. The 10-line `.env` parser in
  `config.py` is the pattern.
- ❌ Don't add ORM models. Use `text(...)` and named parameters.
- ❌ Don't create a `core/`, `lib/`, `utils/`, `common/`, or `helpers/`
  directory. If a helper is generic, inline it.
- ❌ Don't split `extract.py` into `client.py` + `parser.py` unless the file
  exceeds ~400 lines.
- ❌ Don't add migration tooling. Schema changes go in `init_db.py`.
- ❌ Don't add a logging YAML config. The dictConfig in `main.py` is the
  pattern.
- ❌ Don't write a `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, or CI workflow unless explicitly
  asked.
- ❌ Don't generate documentation files (architecture diagrams, ADRs,
  CHANGELOG) unless explicitly asked.

When in doubt, look at the pilot. If the pilot doesn't have it, you probably
don't need it either.
